summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found one unusually direct small-cap public product supplier, PLPC, plus two underfollowed adjacent/direct-customer names, ACA and MYRG, and one diversified reference leader, HUBB. The strongest chokepoint fit is PLPC because its disclosed products include transmission and distribution line support/protection/termination/splicing hardware, while the external search context frames it as a rare public pure-play substitute to private MacLean Power Systems. ACA is an adjacent utility-structures supplier rather than line fittings, but its utility-structures backlog and AI-driven electricity-demand language make it a plausible second-order node beneficiary. MYRG is not a hardware maker; it is included as a direct construction/customer-side signal for transmission and distribution activity that may pull hardware demand forward. HUBB is a diversified public reference leader in utility solutions and transmission/substation components, but less pure. Expanded the universe around the transmission-hardware chokepoint with a two-lane funnel. Reference lane: Hubbell as the diversified public incumbent for utility T&D components. Underfollowed lane: Preformed Line Products as the closest US-listed pure-play line-hardware candidate; Arcosa and Valmont as adjacent transmission-structure and substation-hardware suppliers whose exposure may be one step away from conductor fittings but still tied to line-construction bill-of-material constraints.
